answer.rationale: The security patch cannot be rolled back (constraint from compliance), eliminating rollback_release. Regional failover (memory_b2) addressed a prior degraded region but here the write path itself is 5x p99 across the board; shifting traffic does not add write capacity. Enabling circuit breakers (memory_b4) would shed load/fail fast, which contradicts the objective of not losing customer writes at settlement peak. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) helps dashboard/reporting load but the bottleneck is on the write path. Adding capacity (memory_b3: provisioning headroom absorbed a retail peak with flat queue depth) directly addresses the write-path latency spike during the settlement peak without touching the release or shedding writes. One intervention, sustained availability, no customer-write loss.
